- 10.10 In the `TopicServer` implementation shown in Figures 10.9 and 10.10 on pages 459 and 460, the `receive` method invokes each subscriber’s `receive` method. This means the `TopicServer` ’s `receive` method will not return to its caller until after all of the subscribers have received the message. Consider an alternative version of the `TopicServer` , in which the `receive` method simply places the message into a temporary holding area and hence can quickly return to its caller. Meanwhile, a separate thread running in the `TopicServer` repeatedly loops, retrieving messages from the holding area and sending each in turn to the subscribers. What Java class from Chapter 4 would be appropriate to use for the holding area?
